subject: Unexpected August overage — proposal for remediation and term rollforward
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex@aurora-systems.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected August overage — need reconciliation

Hi Irene,

We just received the August invoice and it includes a $37,840 overage charge that we weren't expecting. Our team understands some burst usage in early August, but this number looks much higher than the usage reports we have. Can you send the raw per-hour usage for Aug 1–31 and a quick explanation of how the overage was calculated?

I attached the invoice we received (Aurora-Aug-invoice.pdf). We need to resolve this quickly — our finance team is holding payment pending clarification.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Platform Operations
Aurora Systems
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex@aurora-systems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected August overage — need reconciliation

Hi Alex — thanks for flagging and for the invoice. We definitely want to get this sorted quickly.

Next steps from our side: I can share the hourly usage export and the derivation of the overage calculation (how committed capacity, burst thresholds, and rollover were applied). Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow (9/13) at 11:00 PT to walk through the numbers with our sales and billing team?

I don't anticipate this being a long dispute — sometimes a short window of sustained concurrency triggered the overage tier. That said, happy to make accommodations if the calculation looks off.

Attaching: usage_breakdown_aug.csv (will follow up with the detailed export).

Best,
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T12:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected August overage — need reconciliation

Team — forwarding Aurora's invoice and Alex's note. Quick summary: unexpected $37.8k overage in August. Customer says their internal metrics don't match. Finance is holding payment.

Proposed approach for the call with Alex tomorrow:
- Walk them through hourly export and the exact points that crossed burst thresholds.
- If it's an honest one-off spike, propose either a one-time credit or an amortized remediation (credit + top-up commitment).
- Offer a short-term capacity top-up (1.5x current committed pool) for Sept–Nov with a 10% term discount if they sign a 12-month rollforward to cover the additional baseline.

Please confirm numbers you want me to share on the call. Ben, if finance okays a preliminary goodwill credit of up to 30% of the overage while we reconcile, say so — we can finalize after the call. Vivek, FYI in case we need an exec note.

Thanks — IC
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected August overage — need reconciliation

Irene — agree with the approach. From a commercial standpoint I'd propose the following settlement terms we can offer on the call:

1) Goodwill credit: 30% of the overage ($11,352) applied against the August invoice immediately.
2) Amortization: Remaining $26,488 can be amortized over 3 monthly invoices (Sep–Nov) at $8,829/month.
3) Capacity/top-up: Offer a temporary top-up package for Sep–Nov equivalent to 1.5x their current committed pool for a locked monthly rate. If Aurora converts the top-up into a permanent capacity increase with a 12-month commitment, give a 10% discount on the monthly committed rate and include 30% of the one-time credit as a contracted credit (i.e., reduces their first invoice after conversion).
4) DocuSign amendment: we'll send a short amendment (one page) that captures the amortization schedule and the top-up conversion path.

If finance can pre-approve the 30% credit as a one-time goodwill, we can close quickly on the call. Ben — can you confirm the accounting posting and whether we can proceed before the reconciliation completes? Otherwise the credit will need final sign-off which will slow payment.

Irene, I'll be on the call and can present the commercial terms.

— Karthik
From: Alex Turner <alex@aurora-systems.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-13T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected August overage — need reconciliation

Thanks all for the call and for walking us through the usage. The hourly export clarified a large 6‑hour sustained ramp on Aug 17 that pushed us into a higher pricing band; that was an internal job misconfiguration on our side.

Aurora's position: we accept that we consumed the tokens but would appreciate support on the billing impact because this was a configuration error during a release window. We are comfortable with the amortization proposal.

Action items we agree to:
- Redwood issues the 30% goodwill credit against Aug invoice.
- Remaining balance amortized across Sep–Nov as discussed.
- We'll review the DocuSign amendment and sign to accept the amortization schedule; please send it today.

Please send the DocuSign link for the amendment and the revised statement of account.

— Alex
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex@aurora-systems.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-15T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected August overage — proposal for remediation and term rollforward

Alex — thanks, and glad the call helped. Attached is the amendment (proposed-amendment-aurora.pdf) and the DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/AA12345-aurora-amendment.

Ben — please issue the 30% credit ($11,352) against the August invoice and post the amortization schedule to Aurora's account: $8,829 for Sep, Oct, Nov. Also note the conversion path for capacity top-up in the amendment; we'll finalize if they sign.

Alex, once signed we'll confirm the credit postings and updated invoice. Appreciate the collaboration.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
